reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes Forsage BUSD through a matrix-marketing structure where participation and higher-level purchases are tied to earning more money. The speaker says viewers can put "$5 in X3" and that opening "big levels" will produce "a lot of money," while the displayed materials show matrix slots, upgrade payments, team counts, profits, and a personal Forsage link. These features together encourage participation in a recruitment- and tier-dependent earning scheme rather than merely discussing it.

citations.quote: So, plan of X3 means that you put $5 in X3, you got a chair, you got a working point, you got a place where you can work and do marketing in one hour.
Similarly, if you want a lot of money in the forces, you need to open big levels. When you open big levels, you will get a lot of money.

opening.argument: The material does not state that earnings are guaranteed or that every participant will profit. Its language is conditional: the speaker says that someone who wants “a lot of money” needs to open larger levels, rather than promising that a particular viewer will receive money. The presentation also appears to invite scrutiny: search terms shown on screen include whether Forsage is “real or fake” and “safe or not.” That context supports treating the video as an explanatory discussion requiring independent judgment, not as an unconditional guarantee. The supplied evidence contains no explicit promise of a fixed return, no assurance of safety, and no instruction to surrender credentials.

citations.quote: Similarly, if you want a lot of money in the forces, you need to open big levels.
Forsage BUSD Online Earning Platform works on a Decentralized + Blockchain system by Mehar Waqas

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution treats the conditional discussion of larger levels as a guarantee, but the quoted language does not promise a fixed return or say that viewers will certainly profit. The frame cited by the prosecution shows a platform screen, yet it does not establish what the speaker is asking viewers to do, whether the figures are examples, or whether the material includes warnings elsewhere. A branded interface alone cannot prove deceptive solicitation.

citations.quote: When you open big levels, you will get a lot of money.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The speaker does more than discuss abstract risk: he directly explains putting money into X3 and connects larger levels with obtaining “a lot of money.” The displayed interface reinforces that the discussion concerns upgrades and balances, not merely a safety investigation. Search queries about whether something is safe do not constitute a warning from the creator, and the absence of a fixed-return promise does not remove the earnings solicitation.

citations.quote: So, plan of X3 means that you put $5 in X3
When you open big levels, you will get a lot of money.

opening.argument: The supplied material can reasonably be read as a tutorial or operational demonstration of how the Forsage interface works. The title identifies an “Online Earning Platform” and describes its decentralized and blockchain basis, while the frames show a matrix-marketing explanation, interface screens with “Preview” and “Upgrade” controls, and a participants list. The speaker explains concepts such as an X3 plan, a working point, and opening levels; that is instructional language about platform operation. No supplied text explicitly says “join now,” requests credentials, or identifies a specific viewer who must pay. Demonstrating a system and describing its mechanics does not by itself establish that the creator is certifying the system or guaranteeing an outcome.

citations.quote: Forsage BUSD Online Earning Platform works on a Decentralized + Blockchain system by Mehar Waqas
So, plan of X3 means that you put $5 in X3, you got a chair, you got a working point, you got a place where you can work and do marketing in one hour.

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the material a demonstration does not explain the speaker’s own earnings-oriented framing. He tells viewers what happens when they put money into X3 and says that opening larger levels produces more money. The interface is not a neutral software tutorial: it visibly contains upgrade amounts and earning figures. Those details make the operational explanation directly relevant to participation and returns.

citations.quote: When you open big levels, you will get a lot of money.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The tutorial framing cannot overcome the content’s stated purpose. The speaker describes paying into X3, marketing, larger levels, and resulting money, while the visuals show Forsage X3/X4 structures and upgrade controls. A demonstration can still promote the demonstrated scheme; the lack of a literal “join now” command does not negate the financial invitation conveyed by these explanations.

citations.quote: you got a place where you can work and do marketing in one hour

opening.argument: The evidence does not establish the specific mechanism required to call this a scam rather than promotion of an online service. The title presents it as a decentralized blockchain platform, and the speech describes a $5 X3 entry as providing a working point and a place to do marketing. Even the prosecution’s visual evidence does not, by itself, prove that the balances are real money received by the speaker, that participants must recruit a downline, or that anyone is guaranteed a return. The supplied material shows platform functions and level options, but no credential request, no verified loss, and no independently established deception. At most, it shows a paid online earning service whose safety and value require separate verification.

citations.quote: works on a Decentralized + Blockchain system
you put $5 in X3, you got a chair, you got a working point, you got a place where you can work and do marketing in one hour.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The missing-mechanism argument overlooks the mechanism stated in the video itself: money is placed into X3, and the speaker says that opening larger levels yields more money. The visuals show upgrade prices alongside X4 and other levels, plus a participant list. The evidence therefore does not depict an ordinary retail purchase with a separately delivered product; it depicts paid progression within a multi-person earning structure.

citations.quote: When you open big levels, you will get a lot of money.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The defense cannot turn explicit paid progression into ordinary commerce merely by calling it a service. The speaker links the $5 X3 payment to a working point and marketing, then links larger levels to more money. The screen shows upgrade prices and balances, while the participant screen shows a group structure. Those facts establish the recruitment- and level-dependent earnings mechanism even without a credential request or independently verified loss.
